answers.question: How long before I can run again? A friend wants me to race the Thanksgiving 10K in five weeks.
answers.answer:
**How long before you can run again:** Short easy runs can start on Tue Oct 20, as the plan shows, if stairs feel easier by then. Plan on about three weeks before any harder running, which puts it around the week of Nov 9 – 15.

**The Thanksgiving 10K in five weeks:** I would not enter it as a race yet. If your easy runs feel normal by the week of Nov 2 – 8, a 10K run at easy effort, not race effort, could fit late in November. We will decide at that check-in.

new.analysis:
## The taper
The last week went exactly as written. Every run landed within a few hundredths of a mile of the plan, and the Wednesday workout held marathon pace at 8:34/mi. Nothing was skipped or overrun, so there is no correction to make.

## The race
You went out on goal pace and held it to about mile 20, which is the right way to run the first half. The goal needed 8:35/mi for the full distance, so the table shows where the time went.

| Stretch | Average pace | Against the 8:35/mi goal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Miles 1 to 20.5 | 8:33/mi | 2 s/mi faster |
| Miles 20.5 to 26.2 | 9:28/mi | about 53 s/mi slower |

The last 5.7 miles cost about five minutes, which is the whole gap to the goal. The most likely cause is long-run volume. The race moved two weeks earlier, so your build was shorter than planned: your longest run was 20 miles, once, and never the 22 you wanted. A fade after 20 miles usually means the legs have not run that far at race pace, so the next block needs longer runs with race-pace work in them.

## Recovery
Your sleep averaged 6.5 hours last week, down from 7.5 the week before. Most recovery happens during sleep, so it matters more than any run this week. Quads and calves are very sore and stairs are hard, which is common this soon after 26 miles. The toe blister should stay clean and covered, and get it checked if it starts to change.

## Why this plan
The next two weeks are recovery only, so every run stays short and easy. A heart rate cap of 130 bpm keeps the effort truly easy, since your easy runs sat near 139 bpm before the race. This week is about 12 miles of running plus one 30-minute walk, under a third of last week's 41 miles, which gives the legs room to repair.

Keep both rest days. If stairs or calves get worse rather than better during a run, stop and walk home.

## What comes next
Tell me what you want to race next: a spring marathon, a half marathon or a shorter race. The answer sets the build we start in two weeks, and it also decides the 10K question.

safetyCallouts.title: One-sided calf swelling needs a same-day check.
safetyCallouts.body: Sore calves are common after a marathon, but a calf that becomes swollen, warm or tender on one side needs a doctor the same day. Chest pain or sudden shortness of breath needs urgent care now, not a run.
